newsitem.title: USA: NYC Hevesi warns of potential for inventory theft.
newsitem.headline: NYC Hevesi warns of potential for inventory theft.

text.p: New York City Comptroller on Monday warned that millions of dollars of equipment and supplies could disappear from some city warehouses and thefts would not be detected due to mismanaged systems.
Hevesi, in prepared remarks, said auditors found almost $2 million in supplies for three city agencies that were listed in inventory records but not stored in warehouses.

"Each year, the city carries close to $200 million worth of materials and supplies in storage, representing a very significant investment on the city's part. We cannot afford to treat this investment in such a cavalier fashion," he said.

He called for a complete overhaul of the Department of Housing Preservation and Development's inventory system, and recommended big improvements in similar systems at the Department of Parks and Recreation, and the Human Resources Administration. But a fourth audit praised the Department of Sanitation for its well-managed inventory operations.
